<tjsInfo:
    Cute and cuddly in appearance, feral
cats look and seem much like common house
cats, at least from a distance, but can
be very "skittish" and quick to panic and
run off, afraid of and unwanting of any
human petting or otherwise touching them.
They are wild animals that are the same
species as house cats, but were not
raised as domesticated pets, and grew up
in the wilderness without ever getting
used to human touch, care, or affection.
They can and will bite, claw, maul, and
hurt people if they are cornered and feel
they have to defend themselves.  These
specific feral cats are aggressive and
fiesty compared to typical stray or feral
cats, and will attack people in
wilderness areas, regardless of being
smaller than a human being.  Some
theorize that this might have something
to do with the coming of increased
numbers of monsters roaming the
countrysides of Acrydia.
\LB
    Cats are fur-bearing creatures, and
like many other fur-bearing creatures are
vulnerable to elemental fire, as their
fur will catch on fire and burn quite
painfully under exposure to such
things.
\LB
    Like all non-sentient wildlife of
Acrydia, and other worlds, cats have
their own natural spirit, and therefore
at least a small amount of magic points
generated by their spirit, although
common feral cats don't have
magical powers or the sentient
intelligence to cast spells or use any of
their spirit for any magical purpose.
>

<tjsInfo:
Even though wolves are dog-like canines,
this particular animal is not just an
animal, but a wild animal, and no matter
how much of a dog-lover or animal-lover
type you may be, it isn't exactly itching
to be your new, faithful pet doggy
and companion, and doesn't exactly want
to play fetch or cuddle up with you, or
anything else pet-doggy-like that it and
the next wolf wouldn't take to kindly to.
It is in fact a very wild and potentially
dangerous and ferocious animal that can
and will hurt you, biting off parts of
you if it can, and it doesn't exactly
feel guilty if it kills you in some 
violent and un-pet-doggy-like act that
it will do without hesitation.  Needless
to say, if you call out "Here doggy
doggy..." and it runs toward you, it
isn't running to you to give you a big
hug.  The growling and snarling stuff is
also kind of a big hint, something of a
giveaway of what it intends to do to you.

the wilderness, and quite dangerous.

provoke it, leave it alone, and don't
you dare entertain the idea of finding
out what it would be like to pet the fur
coat of one.  It has it's own ideas about

very much.

<tjsInfo:
Ladies and Gents, we have a bear.  This
one has nothing "teddy" about it, so go
ahead and forget about any fuzzy, cuddly
thoughts revolving around cuteness or
warm fuzzy comfort of any kind or sort.
Also, this isn't the little-kid storybook
cartoon sort that dresses up in human
clothes and goes shopping with a family
in some childhood cartoon story.  Don't
bother trying to compare it with any
televised version of such a cartoon
either.  It just won't work, and this
bear isn't up for such a thing.
\LB
    This bear is a wild animal.  It is
also a rather large-sized creature of
meat and muscle, a lot of muscle in
particular, which is quite capable of
ripping flesh and bone with a mighty yet
casual swipe of one of it's legs, paws,
and claws.  It can and will rip to
shreds, crush, and eat any typical
puny-in-comparison frail, weak, flimsy,
and fleshy thing such as, gosh, a human
being?

something warm and furry, and perhaps
large like this animal, that you could
give a big hug and live to tell about it,
you want a large sized "teddy" type of
bear, not this one.  No really, the teddy
is what you want for that, while this one
is the one that kills and eats you.  Get
it?  Got it?  Good.
